title: Numbers Chapter 35 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Numbers chapter 35 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Numbers Chapter 35 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Numbers Chapter 35.

questions.question: Where did the LORD speak unto Moses as recorded in Numbers 35:1?
options: In the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho
On Mount Sinai
In the wilderness of Zin
By the Red Sea
questions.correctAnswer: In the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:1 states that the LORD spake unto Moses in the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho.

questions.question: To whom were the children of Israel commanded to give cities to dwell in?
options: The Levites
The priests
The elders
The children of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: The Levites
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:2 commands the children of Israel to give cities to the Levites to dwell in.

questions.question: According to Numbers 35:3, what were the suburbs of the Levites' cities intended for?
options: For their cattle, goods, and all their beasts
For building altars
For planting vineyards
For military training
questions.correctAnswer: For their cattle, goods, and all their beasts
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:3 states the suburbs around the cities were for the Levites' cattle, goods, and all their beasts.

questions.question: How far from the city wall were the suburbs to extend around the Levites' cities?
options: One thousand cubits
Five hundred cubits
Two thousand cubits
Three thousand cubits
questions.correctAnswer: One thousand cubits
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:4 commands that the suburbs shall reach from the city wall outward a thousand cubits.

questions.question: What measurement was given for the suburbs on each side of the city according to Numbers 35:5?
options: Two thousand cubits on each side
One thousand cubits on each side
Three thousand cubits on each side
Five hundred cubits on each side
questions.correctAnswer: Two thousand cubits on each side
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:5 instructs to measure two thousand cubits on the east, south, west, and north sides of the city for the suburbs.

questions.question: How many cities for refuge were to be appointed among the cities given to the Levites?
options: Six
Twelve
Three
Forty-eight
questions.correctAnswer: Six
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:6 states that among the cities given to the Levites, six shall be cities for refuge.

questions.question: What is the total number of cities to be given to the Levites including the cities of refuge?
options: Forty-eight
Forty-two
Six
Fifty-four
questions.correctAnswer: Forty-eight
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:7 says all cities given to the Levites shall be forty-eight, including the six cities of refuge.

questions.question: According to Numbers 35:8, how should the cities be distributed among the children of Israel?
options: According to their inheritance: many for those with many, few for those with few
Equally among all tribes
Only to the tribe of Levi
By random selection
questions.correctAnswer: According to their inheritance: many for those with many, few for those with few
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:8 commands that those with many cities give many, and those with few give few, according to their inheritance.

questions.question: When were the children of Israel to appoint cities of refuge according to Numbers 35:10?
options: When they come over Jordan into the land of Canaan
Immediately after Egypt
While wandering in the wilderness
After conquering Jericho
questions.correctAnswer: When they come over Jordan into the land of Canaan
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:10 instructs the children of Israel to appoint cities of refuge when they come over Jordan into Canaan.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the cities of refuge as described in Numbers 35:11?
options: A place where the slayer may flee who kills unintentionally
A place for worship
A military fortress
A city for the high priest only
questions.correctAnswer: A place where the slayer may flee who kills unintentionally
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:11 says the cities of refuge are for the slayer who kills any person unintentionally to flee to.

questions.question: True or False: The cities of refuge were to protect the manslayer from the avenger until judgment was given.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:12 explains that the cities of refuge protect the manslayer from the avenger until he stands before the congregation for judgment.

questions.question: True or False: According to Numbers 35:1, the LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:1 states the LORD spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho, not in Sinai.

questions.question: True or False: The Levites were given both cities and the surrounding suburbs to dwell in and keep their cattle.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:2-3 commands that the Levites be given cities to dwell in along with suburbs for their cattle and goods.

questions.question: True or False: The cities of refuge were only for the children of Israel and not for strangers or sojourners.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:15 clarifies that the cities of refuge are for the children of Israel, the stranger, and the sojourner among them.

questions.question: In Numbers 35, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Commanding the children of Israel to give cities to the Levites
Appointing cities of refuge
Measuring the suburbs around the Levites’ cities
Giving six cities for refuge among the Levites’ cities
questions.correctAnswer: Commanding the children of Israel to give cities to the Levites
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:2 is the earliest instruction directing the children of Israel to give cities to the Levites, before measurements or appointing refuge cities.

medium.title: Numbers Chapter 35 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Numbers Chapter 35 to real-life situations.

questions.question: How many cities were designated as cities of refuge according to Numbers 35?
options: Six
Three
Forty-eight
Twelve
questions.correctAnswer: Six
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:13 states that six cities were to be given as cities of refuge. This is reinforced by Numbers 35:14 which specifies three on each side of the Jordan.

questions.question: According to Numbers 35, how are the cities of refuge distributed geographically?
options: Three on this side of Jordan and three in Canaan
All six in Canaan
All six on this side of Jordan
Two on each border of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Three on this side of Jordan and three in Canaan
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:14 clearly directs that three cities be given on this side of Jordan and three in the land of Canaan, making up the six cities of refuge.

questions.question: Who are allowed to flee to the cities of refuge according to Numbers 35?
options: Children of Israel, strangers, and sojourners
Only the children of Israel
Only Levites
Only strangers and sojourners
questions.correctAnswer: Children of Israel, strangers, and sojourners
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:15 states that the cities of refuge are for the children of Israel, the stranger, and the sojourner among them, allowing all these groups refuge if they kill unintentionally.

questions.question: What is the consequence for a person who kills another with an instrument of iron according to Numbers 35?
options: He is a murderer and shall be put to death
He shall flee to a city of refuge
He shall pay a ransom
He shall be forgiven after judgment
questions.correctAnswer: He is a murderer and shall be put to death
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:16 states that if a person kills with an instrument of iron, he is considered a murderer and must be put to death, emphasizing the gravity of intentional killing.

questions.question: According to Numbers 35, what judgment applies to someone who kills another by throwing a stone that causes death?
options: He is a murderer and shall be put to death
He shall be sent to a city of refuge
He shall be fined
He shall be forgiven by the congregation
questions.correctAnswer: He is a murderer and shall be put to death
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:17 specifies that killing by throwing a stone resulting in death classifies the killer as a murderer who must be put to death.

questions.question: What role does the 'revenger of blood' have according to Numbers 35?
options: To kill the murderer when he meets him
To forgive the murderer
To judge the murderer
To exile the murderer
questions.correctAnswer: To kill the murderer when he meets him
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:19 explains that the revenger of blood is to kill the murderer upon meeting him, emphasizing the law of retribution for murder.

questions.question: What distinguishes a murderer acting 'of hatred' from one who kills unintentionally according to Numbers 35?
options: Killing with premeditation or enmity results in death penalty
Killing accidentally leads to death penalty
All killings are treated equally
Only killing with iron instruments is murder
questions.correctAnswer: Killing with premeditation or enmity results in death penalty
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:20-21 clarifies that killing out of hatred or by laying in wait is murder deserving death, contrasting with accidental killing described in later verses.

questions.question: If a person kills without enmity or premeditation, what process does Numbers 35 say should be followed?
options: The congregation shall judge between the slayer and the revenger of blood
The slayer shall be immediately put to death
The slayer shall be forgiven without judgment
The slayer must leave the land permanently
questions.correctAnswer: The congregation shall judge between the slayer and the revenger of blood
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:22-24 instruct that if the killing was without enmity or laying of wait, the congregation must judge between the slayer and the avenger of blood to administer justice properly.

questions.question: What does Numbers 35 say will happen if the congregation rules in favor of the slayer in a manslaughter case?
options: The slayer is delivered to the city of refuge to dwell there until the high priest dies
The slayer is set free immediately
The slayer pays a fine to the family
The slayer is exiled forever
questions.correctAnswer: The slayer is delivered to the city of refuge to dwell there until the high priest dies
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:25 explains the congregation will restore the slayer to the city of refuge where he must remain until the high priest's death, providing protection from vengeance.

questions.question: What consequence does Numbers 35 describe for a slayer who leaves the city of refuge before the death of the high priest?
options: The revenger of blood may kill him without guilt
He is forgiven
He must return immediately
He will face a trial in the congregation
questions.correctAnswer: The revenger of blood may kill him without guilt
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:26-27 states that if the slayer leaves the city of refuge before the high priest's death, the revenger of blood may kill him without being guilty of bloodshed.

questions.question: According to Numbers 35, what happens after the death of the high priest concerning the slayer in the city of refuge?
options: The slayer may return to his land
The slayer must remain in the city forever
The slayer is executed
The slayer is exiled to another country
questions.correctAnswer: The slayer may return to his land
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:28 states that after the death of the high priest, the slayer is permitted to return to the land of his possession, ending his exile.

questions.question: What does Numbers 35:30 require as evidence before a murderer is put to death?
options: The testimony of two or more witnesses
The confession of the murderer
The testimony of one witness
The approval of the revenger of blood
questions.correctAnswer: The testimony of two or more witnesses
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:30 requires at least two witnesses to testify against a person before they can be put to death, ensuring fairness in capital cases.

questions.question: According to Numbers 35, is it permissible to accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who is guilty of death?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:31 explicitly forbids taking any ransom for the life of a murderer guilty of death, indicating the seriousness of the offense.

questions.question: Does Numbers 35 teach that the land is defiled by the shedding of innocent blood?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:33-34 teach that shedding innocent blood defiles the land and that the land can only be cleansed by the blood of the one who shed it, showing God's concern for justice and holiness.

questions.question: According to Numbers 35, what is the role of the congregation in cases of manslaughter?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:24 and 35:25 show that the congregation judges between the slayer and the revenger of blood and delivers the slayer to the city of refuge, playing an active judicial role.

hard.title: Numbers Chapter 35 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Numbers Chapter 35.

questions.question: According to Numbers 35, what must happen when the slayer flees to a city of refuge?
options: He must remain there until the death of the high priest
He is immediately pardoned and can return home
He must stand trial before the congregation immediately
He is handed over to the avenger of blood for punishment
questions.correctAnswer: He must remain there until the death of the high priest
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:25 states that the congregation shall restore the slayer to the city of refuge, where he shall abide until the death of the high priest, indicating a period of protection until then.

questions.question: What happens if the slayer leaves the city of refuge before the death of the high priest and is found by the avenger of blood?
options: The avenger of blood may kill him without guilt
The slayer is protected by the congregation
The slayer must pay a ransom to the avenger
The slayer is to be put on trial again
questions.correctAnswer: The avenger of blood may kill him without guilt
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:27 explains that if the slayer leaves the city of refuge and the avenger finds and kills him, the avenger is not guilty of bloodshed because the slayer should have remained in the city until the high priest's death.

questions.question: What is the significance of the death of the high priest in the laws concerning the city of refuge?
options: It marks the end of the slayer’s exile and he may return home
It initiates a new period of exile for the slayer
It requires the slayer to stand trial again
It has no effect on the slayer’s status
questions.correctAnswer: It marks the end of the slayer’s exile and he may return home
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:28 states that after the death of the high priest, the slayer shall return to his land, marking the end of the refuge period.

questions.question: What does Numbers 35:30 specify about the testimony required to put a murderer to death?
options: The murderer must be convicted by the mouth of witnesses, and one witness is not sufficient
One witness is enough to convict a murderer
No witnesses are required if the murderer confesses
The testimony of the avenger of blood is sufficient
questions.correctAnswer: The murderer must be convicted by the mouth of witnesses, and one witness is not sufficient
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:30 clearly states that a murderer shall be put to death by the testimony of witnesses, but one witness cannot testify to cause death, emphasizing the need for multiple witnesses.

questions.question: What is forbidden according to Numbers 35:31 regarding the life of a murderer?
options: Taking any ransom or satisfaction for the life of the murderer
Allowing the murderer to flee to a city of refuge
Having more than two witnesses against the murderer
Killing the murderer without a trial
questions.correctAnswer: Taking any ransom or satisfaction for the life of the murderer
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:31 forbids taking satisfaction (ransom) for the life of a murderer, stating that the murderer must surely be put to death.

questions.question: How does Numbers 35:33 describe the effect of bloodshed on the land?
options: Bloodshed defiles the land and it cannot be cleansed except by the blood of the one who shed it
Bloodshed has no effect on the land
The land is cleansed by sacrifices made at the temple
Only the high priest can cleanse the land
questions.correctAnswer: Bloodshed defiles the land and it cannot be cleansed except by the blood of the one who shed it
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:33 teaches that bloodshed pollutes the land, and the only way to cleanse it is through the blood of the one who shed it, showing the seriousness of shedding innocent blood.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of sanctuary and refuge for the innocent as found in Numbers 35?
options: Joshua 20
Leviticus 16
Exodus 20
Deuteronomy 6
questions.correctAnswer: Joshua 20
questions.explanation: Joshua 20 details the establishment of cities of refuge in the Promised Land, directly fulfilling and continuing the instructions given in Numbers 35 about providing sanctuary for accidental manslayers.

questions.question: The Hebrew term translated as 'avenger of blood' (רֹצֵחַ) in Numbers 35 refers to what role?
options: A family member who seeks to avenge unlawfully shed blood
A city official who judges murder cases
A priest who performs cleansing rites
A Levite assigned to protect the city gates
questions.correctAnswer: A family member who seeks to avenge unlawfully shed blood
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'roẓeaḥ' (רֹצֵחַ) means 'murderer' or 'avenger of blood,' referring to a relative who is responsible for exacting justice for unlawful killing, as seen in Numbers 35:19.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Numbers 35:25-28 involving the slayer and the city of refuge?
options: Inclusio, framing the legal protection and exile of the slayer
Chiasm, emphasizing the reversal of judgment
Parallelism, contrasting slayer and avenger
Allegory, representing spiritual refuge
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio, framing the legal protection and exile of the slayer
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:25-28 uses inclusio by framing the narrative around the slayer’s protection while in the city of refuge and the consequences of leaving it prematurely, creating a literary frame that highlights exile and safety.

questions.question: According to Numbers 35:34, why is it important not to defile the land where Israel dwells?
options: Because the LORD dwells among the children of Israel in that land
Because the land is the source of Israel’s wealth
Because the land is under a covenant with Abraham
Because the land is surrounded by hostile nations
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD dwells among the children of Israel in that land
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:34 instructs not to defile the land because God Himself dwells among Israel there, indicating the sanctity of the land as His dwelling place.

questions.question: Which of the following is TRUE regarding satisfaction (ransom) for a person who fled to a city of refuge according to Numbers 35:32?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:32 states that no ransom shall be taken for the person who fled to the city of refuge to return to the land until the death of the priest, affirming protection without payment.

questions.question: If a person kills another by throwing a stone intentionally, is he considered a murderer according to Numbers 35?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:17 explicitly states that if a person strikes another with a stone with intent and the person dies, he is a murderer and must be put to death.

questions.question: In Numbers 35:29, what is declared about the statutes concerning manslayers and cities of refuge?
options: They shall be statutes of judgment throughout all generations and dwellings
They apply only to the generation that entered Canaan
They are suggestions rather than commands
They shall be abolished after the priesthood ends
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be statutes of judgment throughout all generations and dwellings
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:29 emphasizes that these laws are enduring statutes for judgment across all generations and places where Israel dwells, highlighting their perpetual significance.

questions.question: How does the law of cities of refuge in Numbers 35 foreshadow New Testament themes?
options: It foreshadows Christ as a refuge for sinners seeking mercy
It predicts the destruction of Jerusalem
It symbolizes the end of the Levitical priesthood
It prefigures the division of the tribes of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows Christ as a refuge for sinners seeking mercy
questions.explanation: The cities of refuge, providing protection and safety for accidental killers, typologically foreshadow Christ who offers refuge and salvation to sinners, as echoed in Hebrews 6:18-20.

questions.question: According to Numbers 35:16-21, what distinguishes a murderer from one who kills unintentionally?
options: Intent and premeditation in the act of killing
The weapon used in the killing
Whether the victim was a stranger or a relative
The location where the killing occurred
questions.correctAnswer: Intent and premeditation in the act of killing
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:16-21 distinguishes murderers as those who kill with intent, hatred, or premeditation, while unintentional killings are handled differently, such as seeking refuge in designated cities.

theological.title: Numbers Chapter 35 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Numbers Chapter 35 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is primarily taught by the instruction to assign cities and their surrounding suburbs to the Levites according to Numbers 35:2-3?
options: The doctrine of God's provision for His priestly servants
The doctrine of salvation by works
The doctrine of eternal punishment
The doctrine of predestination
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of God's provision for His priestly servants
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:2-3 teaches that the Levites are given cities and suburbs for their dwelling and their cattle, showing God's provision and care for His dedicated servants, the Levites, who minister in His name.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by God's command to establish cities of refuge for the manslayer in Numbers 35:11-12?
options: Justice and mercy
Omnipotence
Omniscience
Immutability
questions.correctAnswer: Justice and mercy
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:11-12 shows God's justice in requiring judgment before punishment and His mercy in providing refuge for unintentional killers, balancing both attributes perfectly.

questions.question: How does Numbers 35:6-7, which commands the allocation of six cities of refuge among the Levites' forty-eight cities, relate to God's covenantal faithfulness to Israel?
options: It shows God's provision for justice within the covenant community
It mandates strict punishment without mercy
It establishes a new sacrificial system
It replaces the Mosaic law with a new law
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God's provision for justice within the covenant community
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:6-7 reflects God's faithfulness by providing a just system for manslayers to find refuge, preserving life within His covenant people and upholding holiness.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do Numbers 35:16-18 and 35:20-21 provide about the nature of murder and human responsibility?
options: Murder is a grave sin deserving death, showing human accountability for intentional killing
Murder is excusable under certain circumstances
Killing is always allowed if accidental
All killing is forbidden without exception
questions.correctAnswer: Murder is a grave sin deserving death, showing human accountability for intentional killing
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:16-18 and 35:20-21 make clear that intentional killing with malice, hatred, or premeditation is murder and requires death, emphasizing human responsibility for such acts.

questions.question: According to Numbers 35:22-25, what theological principle is illustrated by the congregation's role in judging the slayer and revenger of blood?
options: The principle of communal justice and due process
The principle of individualism without accountability
The principle of arbitrary punishment
The principle of forgiveness without judgment
questions.correctAnswer: The principle of communal justice and due process
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:22-25 shows that the congregation must judge fairly between parties, illustrating God's design for communal justice and due process in society.

questions.question: What narrative arc does Numbers 35:10-15 contribute to the grand biblical story?
options: The establishment of God's holy order protecting the innocent within the Promised Land
The fall of man into sin
The final judgment of the world
The creation of the universe
questions.correctAnswer: The establishment of God's holy order protecting the innocent within the Promised Land
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:10-15 advances the narrative of God's covenantal provision for justice and mercy by instituting cities of refuge to protect accidental killers in the Promised Land.

questions.question: How does Numbers 35:33-34 reveal God's concern for holiness and the sanctification of the land Israel will inhabit?
options: God commands that the land not be polluted by bloodshed because He dwells among His people
God allows defilement of the land as a sign of His anger
God is indifferent to the moral condition of the land
God requires frequent sacrifices to cleanse the land
questions.correctAnswer: God commands that the land not be polluted by bloodshed because He dwells among His people
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:33-34 emphasizes God's holiness and His dwelling presence, forbidding blood pollution to keep the land sanctified for His people.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the law of cities of refuge promotes a primitive form of justice that lacks fairness. What does Numbers 35:24-28 actually teach about God's justice in this system?
options: God's justice includes protection for accidental killers balanced with accountability until the death of the high priest
God permits arbitrary killing without trial
God condones vengeance without limits
God does not care about fairness
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice includes protection for accidental killers balanced with accountability until the death of the high priest
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:24-28 teaches a fair judicial system where accidental killers are protected but must remain in refuge until the high priest's death, showing balanced divine justice and mercy.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted by the rule in Numbers 35:30-31 that requires two or more witnesses to put a murderer to death and forbids accepting ransom for one guilty of death?
options: God's righteousness and holiness
God's omnipotence
God's patience
God's wrath
questions.correctAnswer: God's righteousness and holiness
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:30-31 reveals God's righteous and holy nature by insisting on strict evidentiary standards for capital cases and forbidding corruption or ransom for murderers.

questions.question: Combining Numbers 35:4-5 and 35:8, what theological understanding do these verses convey about the distribution of land and the Levites' inheritance?
options: God's equitable distribution respecting individual inheritances while providing for the Levites
God's random allotment of land
God's rejection of the Levites from inheritance
God's command for the Levites to purchase land
questions.correctAnswer: God's equitable distribution respecting individual inheritances while providing for the Levites
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:4-5 and 35:8 show God's justice in measuring suburbs around cities and requiring each tribe to give cities to Levites proportionally to their inheritance, ensuring fairness and provision.

questions.question: What does Numbers 35:19 teach about the role of the avenger of blood in God's justice system, and what does this reveal about divine justice?
options: The avenger of blood is responsible for executing justice upon the murderer, showing God's allowance of familial justice
The avenger of blood must forgive immediately
The avenger of blood can act without judgment
The avenger of blood is irrelevant
questions.correctAnswer: The avenger of blood is responsible for executing justice upon the murderer, showing God's allowance of familial justice
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:19 appoints the avenger of blood to kill the murderer, revealing God's establishment of a justice system that includes family responsibility for avenging unlawful death.

questions.question: How do Numbers 35:29-31 collectively affirm the doctrine of the rule of law and the sanctity of human life in Israel's society?
options: They establish statutes ensuring fair judicial procedures and the sanctity of life with strict penalties for murder
They permit arbitrary killings without evidence
They allow ransom for any crime
They abolish capital punishment
questions.correctAnswer: They establish statutes ensuring fair judicial procedures and the sanctity of life with strict penalties for murder
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:29-31 enshrine just statutes requiring witnesses and forbidding ransom for murderers, upholding the sanctity of life and a lawful society.

questions.question: Which combined divine attributes are revealed in Numbers 35:13-15 concerning the six cities of refuge for both Israelites and strangers?
options: God's impartiality and mercy
God's jealousy and wrath
God's sovereignty and wrath
God's omniscience and omnipotence
questions.correctAnswer: God's impartiality and mercy
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:13-15 shows God’s impartiality by providing refuge for Israelites and strangers alike, and His mercy by protecting unintentional killers.

questions.question: What theological insight emerges from combining Numbers 35:25 and Numbers 35:28 regarding the slayer's stay in the city of refuge and the significance of the high priest's death?
options: The death of the high priest symbolizes atonement allowing the slayer to return home, illustrating God's provision for forgiveness and restoration
The slayer is free immediately upon arrival
The slayer must remain in refuge forever
The high priest's death has no effect on the slayer
questions.correctAnswer: The death of the high priest symbolizes atonement allowing the slayer to return home, illustrating God's provision for forgiveness and restoration
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:25 and 35:28 teach that the slayer remains protected until the high priest dies, indicating that the priest’s death represents atonement and restoration for the offender.

questions.question: What narrative connection does Numbers 35:1-2 establish in the broader redemptive history of Israel as they prepare to enter Canaan?
options: It marks God's preparation for Israel's holy life and worship in the Promised Land
It recounts Israel's wilderness wanderings
It describes the building of the tabernacle
It tells of the conquest of Jericho
questions.correctAnswer: It marks God's preparation for Israel's holy life and worship in the Promised Land
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:1-2 occurs as God commands Moses to assign cities to the Levites in Moab, preparing Israel for a sanctified communal and worship life in Canaan, advancing the redemptive narrative.
